column1: # Donkey Kong Bananza on Android (keys in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Game profiles on Android"). A Switch 2 game (NVN2, Ampere shaders, SDK 20.5.19 Ounce) packed from its NUP.
# 2026-11-07, AYN Odin 3 (Snapdragon 8 Elite, Adreno 830, stock driver 512.800.72): boots from the NUP without a heap check, resumes its save into the mining tunnel; DK, the loose rocks, HUD and
# prompts draw at 30-40 fps (frame work about 21 ms, GPU about 26 ms). Open: the terrain colour pass (raw global memory stores, shaders.md), the main menu art, the game's 9 GB pool on a 12 GB device.

column1: # agl's NDSR upscaler network (24 tensor-core compute kernels, shader_map.tsv agl_ndsr.pck): no DLSS on Android. The replay skips their dispatches and scales the 1536x864 colour input
# into the 2304x1296 output bilinearly (gfx_vk_exec.c upscaler_replace); the game composes from that output. The network left the output untouched here: a flat (0.3, 0.3, 1) frame
# Handheld mode: the game then targets 1080p (Bananza: a 1920x1080 window with a 1048x590 render target) instead of its docked 2880x1620 / 2304x1296 on this 1080p screen.
# Odin 3, Bananza tunnel: frame time p50 33 → 17 ms, p95 36 → 35 ms (with the GPU floor below)
# The Adreno governor parks at 660 MHz under a steady load; the 967 MHz floor (through su, Magisk) cut p95 frame time 47 → 36 ms in the docked tunnel
